keyMissing: The key record is missing; the info attribute is all that is left.
rotateServiceTitle: Makes new random keys at kvno {kvno} and shows their keytab once, with the kvno it replaces still in it. Tickets already issued under the current key go on being accepted for krb5.retainedKeyTtlS.
dropServiceTitle: Stops accepting tickets under kvno {list} now, rather than when their window ends. The current key is untouched.
deleteServiceTitle: Removes the stored key and every previous version. Tickets for this SPN are then keyed as they were before a key was stored.
noServices: No service principal holds a stored key.
notCurrentTitle: The password on the entry is not the one these keys were derived from, so the KDC refuses them. The next verified sign-in derives new ones.
clearPersonTitle: Removes this person's Kerberos keys, previous versions included. Their next AS-REQ is refused with "sign in once"; their next verified sign-in derives new keys at the next kvno.
dropPersonTitle: Stops accepting tickets sealed under kvno {list} — this person's keys before their last password change — now. Their current keys, and so their sign-in, are untouched.
nobodyProduct: Nobody holds Kerberos keys yet. A person gets them the first time their password is set or verified.
nobodyDevelopment: Development mode keys every user from krb5.userPassword, so nobody here holds stored keys.
srcStored: a random key stored on the directory
srcUnreadable: a record this service cannot open
krbtgtIntro: Every ticket-granting ticket this realm issues is sealed under this key.
krbtgtPassword: In this development realm it is derived from the published krb5.krbtgtPassword, so a reader can decrypt a TGT; rotating it here replaces it with a random stored key.
krbtgtRandom1: It is a RANDOM key per enctype, kept sealed on the directory entry
krbtgtRandom2: and never shown — there is no keytab for it.
krbtgtRotation: A rotation keeps the version it replaces for {ttl} seconds (the longest a TGT under it can live, renewals included), so every TGT goes on working; rotate and invalidate keeps nothing — Active Directory's double reset in one act — and every TGT in the realm is refused at its next use.
unreadable1: The stored krbtgt key cannot be opened here (
unreadable2: ), so this KDC issues no ticket. Only rotate and invalidate replaces it.
noneStored: No krbtgt key is stored for this realm yet, so its KDC issues no ticket. It is made at the next start, or by the krb5.krbtgt-rotate job, or by a rotation here.
rotateKrbtgtTitle: A new random krbtgt key at the next kvno; the current one is kept for the TGTs already sealed under it. Queued on the scheduler.
dropKrbtgtTitle: Stops accepting TGTs sealed under kvno {list} now. The current key is untouched.
typeConfirm2: to end every TGT in the realm
needWriteKrbtgt: Rotating the krbtgt key needs Admin Write.
whoFor: Who this KDC holds a stored key for.
noKey: No key is on this page, and none is in its JSON.
ttlZero: (the ticket lifetime plus the clock skew, because krb5.retainedKeyTtlS is 0)
acceptor: The acceptor on krb5.servicePort and /authn/spnego answers as
acceptorStored: , keyed from a service principal stored here.
acceptorPassword: , keyed from krb5.servicePassword. Creating that SPN here gives it a random key and a keytab instead.
acceptorNone: , and holds no key: create that SPN here to give it one.
create1: A service principal name — HTTP/web.example.com, with or without
create2: . It gets a RANDOM key for every enctype in krb5.enctypes (never rc4-hmac in product mode) at kvno {kvno}, stored sealed on its application entry, and the next page shows its keytab ONCE. krbtgt is refused: it has its own block above, and no keytab.
needWriteServices: Creating, rotating and deleting a service principal needs Admin Write.
hNoButton: What there is deliberately no button for
noButton: Downloading a keytab again. A stored key is never read back out: a service principal's keytab is handed over by the create or rotate that made it, and a lost one is replaced by rotating. A PERSON's keytab (#59) is derived from a password in hand: Reset password and download keytab on their page under Directory → Users, or their own password on /portal/kerberos. Setting a person's keys. They come from the person's password and from nothing else; clearing them is the one control, and the next verified sign-in derives them again.
linkApi: the same over the management API
